chapter: Politics, bebop and the small-band years
title: Latin rhythms, Machito and Mario Bauza
summary: Crawford says Lunceford played little Latin music, and recalls Machito and trumpeter Mario Bauza.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: When did you start playing Latin type rhythms in the '30s? Is that when they started having a --
Yeah, revolutionizing, putting it all in there.
Well, there was a period when --
Sambas and mambas and all that kind of stuff.
No, not to us. Not to us. Not Jimmy Lunceford. He didn't play much of that.
Did many bands play much of that? Because, I saw a movie with --
Well, you had bands. You had Machito and renaissance and all those things. That was on the bandstand at one time?
Mario Bauza (Unintelligible), do you remember his band?
Yeah, I heard him, he was a good trumpet player. Wasn't he a trumpet player?
Yeah, Dizzy used to go and sit in.
Yeah, Mario was a good, legitimate trumpet player. Oh, yes.
